title: It's raining, so I haven't left yet
title_target: မိုးရွာနေတယ်၊ ဒါကြောင့် မထွက်သေးဘူး — moh:-ywa-nay-dè, da-chowⁿ. ma.htwèk-thay:-boo:
goal: Saying that something is happening right now, has already happened, or hasn't happened yet — three states that Burmese marks with three small words that are easy to mix up.
bekal: using …နေတယ် for something happening right now
using …ပြီ for a situation that has just changed
using မ…သေးဘူး for something that hasn't happened yet
telling apart ပြီ and ပြီး, which sound alike
answering the phone and explaining what you're doing

dialogs.title: စကားပြော — A phone call on a rainy morning
dialogs.intro: Ko Zaw calls Ani, who hasn't reached the office yet. Watch for three different small words: နေ for what is in progress, ပြီ for a situation that has just changed, and သေး for what hasn't happened yet.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ဟယ်လို|hè-loh] [အာနီ|a-nee]၊ [ဘယ်မှာ|bè-hma] [လဲ|lè:]။ [ဘာ|ba] [လုပ်|lohk] [နေ|nay] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: Hello Ani, where are you? What are you doing?
lines.literal: hello — ani, where-at — Q? what — do — -ing — Q?

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [အိမ်မှာ|ayⁿ-hma] [ရှိ|shee.] [သေး|thay:] [တယ်|dè]။ [မိုး|moh:] [ရွာ|ywa] [နေ|nay] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.literal: home-at — be — still — statement. rain — fall — -ing — statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [မထွက်သေးဘူး|ma.htwèk-thay:-boo:]။ [မနက်စာ|ma.nèk-sa] [စား|sa:] [နေ|nay] [တယ်|dè]။

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ကောင်း|kowⁿ:] [ပါပြီ|ba-bee]။ [အစည်းအဝေး|a.see:-a.way:] [စ|sa.] [ပြီ|bee]၊ [ဒါပေမဲ့|da-bay-mè.] [အရေးမကြီးဘူး|a.yay:-ma.chee:-boo:]။
lines.id: All right. The meeting has started, but it's not that important.
lines.literal: good — polite-already. meeting — start — already, but — important-not-big.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [တောင်းပန်|towⁿ:-paⁿ] [ပါတယ်|ba-dè]။ [ဘယ်နှစ်နာရီ|bè-hna.na-yee] [စ|sa.] [လဲ|lè:]။
lines.id: Sorry. What time does it start?

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ကိုးနာရီ|koh:-na-yee] [စ|sa.] [တယ်|dè]။ [အခု|a.hkoo.] [ဒေါ်ခင်|dò-hkiⁿ] [ပြော|pyò:] [နေ|nay] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: It starts at nine. Daw Khin is speaking now.
lines.literal: nine-o'clock — start — statement. now — daw-khin — speak — -ing — statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဒါဆို|da-hsoh] [ခုနစ်|hkoo.nik] [မိနစ်|mee.nik] [အတွင်း|a.twiⁿ:] [ရောက်|yowk] [မယ်|mè]။ [တက္ကစီ|tèk-ka.see] [ခေါ်|hkò] [ပြီးပြီ|pyee:-bee]။
lines.id: Then I'll be there within seven minutes. I've already called a taxi.
lines.literal: in-that-case — seven — minute — within — arrive — will. taxi — call — done-already.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]။ [မိုး|moh:] [တိတ်|tayk] [ပြီ|bee] [လား|la:]။

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [တိတ်|tayk] [ပြီ|bee]။ [အခု|a.hkoo.] [နေ|nay] [ထွက်|htwèk] [နေ|nay] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: It's stopped. Now the sun is coming out.
lines.literal: stop — already. now — sun — come-out — -ing — statement.

lines.speaker: ကိုဇော်:
lines.text: [ကောင်း|kowⁿ:] [တာပေါ့|da-baw.]။ [ဖြေးဖြေး|hpyay:-hpyay:] [လာ|la] [ပါ|ba]၊ [လမ်း|laⁿ:] [ချော်|hchaw] [နေ|nay] [တယ်|dè]။
lines.id: Good. Take it slow, the roads are slippery.
lines.literal: good — of-course. slowly-slowly — come — polite, road — slippery — -ing — statement.

lines.speaker: အာနီ:
lines.text: [ဟုတ်ကဲ့|hohk-kè.]၊ [ကျေးဇူးတင်ပါတယ်|chay:-zoo:-tiⁿ-ba-dè]။ [ခဏနေ|hka.na.-nay] [တွေ့|tway.] [မယ်|mè]။

grammars.title: …နေတယ် — happening right now
body: နေ (*nay*) goes right before the sentence ending and turns it into "-ing", something in progress. It looks exactly like the verb နေတယ် "to stay, live" — and that's where it comes from: "is eating" is literally "stays in the state of eating".

head: Without နေ
With နေ
Say it
Meaning
rows: မိုးရွာတယ်
မိုးရွာနေတယ်
ဘာလုပ်နေလဲ

after: ⚠️ Don't use နေ just because your sentence is about the present. Everyday habits keep plain တယ်: နေ့တိုင်း ကော်ဖီ သောက်တယ် (I drink coffee every day), not သောက်နေတယ်. နေ is only for what is **really going on at that very moment**.

grammars.title: …ပြီ — the situation has just changed
body: ပြီ (*bee*) replaces the ending တယ် and means "already, at last". It doesn't simply mark the past — it says that **the situation has moved from "not yet" to "now it is"**.

head: Burmese
Say it
Meaning
What it implies
rows: before, I was on the way
အသက် ဆယ့်ခြောက်နှစ် ရှိပြီ
ထွက်ပြီလား

after: ⚠️ **ပြီ and ပြီး are different.** ပြီ (level tone, *bee*) means "already"; ပြီး (high tone, *pyee:*) means "done, and then" and links two events: စားပြီးတော့ သွားမယ် (after eating, I'll go). They sound almost the same but mean very different things — this is why tones matter.

grammars.title: မ…သေးဘူး — not yet
body: For "not yet", သေး (*thay:*) slots into the negative frame you already know: မ … သေး … ဘူး. This is the direct partner of ပြီ, and the two often turn up in the same conversation.

head: Question
"Yes, already"
"Not yet"
rows: ထွက်ပြီလား
မထွက်သေးဘူး — *ma.htwèk-thay:-boo:*
မစားသေးဘူး
မရောက်သေးဘူး

after: သေး can also stand in a positive sentence with the meaning "still": အိမ်မှာ ရှိသေးတယ် (still at home). So this one word covers both "still" and "not yet", depending on whether the sentence is positive or negative.

grammars.title: Answering the phone
body: Phone calls have a few set phrases worth memorizing whole — on the phone there are no hand gestures to help you out.

head: Burmese
Say it
English
rows: ခဏ စောင့်ပါ
နောက်မှ ဖုန်းဆက်မယ်

after: ⚠️ People in Myanmar often open a call with ဟယ်လို and then say their own name straight away, without waiting to be asked. Giving your name first is considered polite and saves a round of back-and-forth.

blocks.text: The words learned today all sit in the same place in the sentence — right before the ending — so they're easy to mix up. The table below puts them side by side so you can see the difference at a glance.

head: Word
Say it
Meaning
Example
rows: စားနေတယ် — is eating
စားပြီ — have eaten
မစားသေးဘူး — haven't eaten yet
ရှိသေးတယ် — is still there
စားပြီးတော့ — after eating
စားဖူးတယ် — have eaten (it) before

blocks.text: Notice that **not one** of the six changes the form of the verb. စား stays စား in every row. This is the promise made in the introduction: Burmese has no verb tables to memorize, only endings to attach.

blocks.title: The most useful five-minute drill
items: Take one verb — say, သွား (go) — and say all six forms in a row: သွားနေတယ်၊ သွားပြီ၊ မသွားသေးဘူး၊ သွားသေးတယ်၊ သွားပြီးတော့၊ သွားဖူးတယ်။
Repeat with စား၊ လုပ်၊ ဝယ်၊ ပြော. Five verbs times six forms makes thirty sentences, all coming out of one table you already have.
